label: STOPP K7: opioid with recurrent falls
title: Opioid in a person who falls
statement: Opioids in patients with recurrent falls (may impair sensorium).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: Opioids can cause drowsiness and dizziness, which raises the risk of falling in a person who already falls often.

medicine_groups.name: Systemic opioids
medicine_groups.note: Oral and sublingual products, patches, suppositories and injections count. Suboxone contains buprenorphine and naloxone. Bupradex is a buprenorphine tablet. Proladone is an oxycodone suppository. The three listed pethidine names identify injection packs. Targin is oxycodone with naloxone. Panadeine Forte is paracetamol with codeine, Nurofen Plus is ibuprofen with codeine and Mersyndol is paracetamol with codeine and doxylamine. Opioid medicines used for dependence treatment may also be listed here. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. Include dihydrocodeine cough liquid and other systemic opioids regardless of indication.

needs_facts.meets: Two or more falls in the past 12 months counted back from the latest date in the record, or a documented diagnosis of recurrent falls.

options.words: Two or more falls in the past 12 months
One fall in the past 12 months and no diagnosis of recurrent falls
No falls in the past 12 months and no diagnosis of recurrent falls

rule_for_models: For a Group A opioid supply, report no finding if age is under 65. At age 65 or older, report a finding and cite the supply and falls evidence if the record shows two or more falls in the past 12 months counted back from the latest date in the record, or a documented diagnosis of recurrent falls. A documented diagnosis qualifies even if fewer than two falls are reported. Report no finding when the history confirms zero or one fall in that period and there is no documented diagnosis of recurrent falls. If the falls history for that period is missing or unknown and no diagnosis is established, cite the supply and report only a possible finding naming Recurrent falls. If age is missing and the other conditions are met, report only a possible finding and ask for the age. If falls history is also missing, name both age and Recurrent falls.
cannot_be_seen: How often the opioid is really taken, whether the person still uses it, the cause and number of any falls, other sedating medicines bought without a prescription, and the reason for treatment.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether the opioid is still needed and at the lowest effective dose for a person with recurrent falls.
